text:
kevin (pm): Quick sync — Q4 roadmap decisions for the Optimize toolkit + evals. We have three customer-driven asks on the table: 1) actionable batching/caching recommendations in the Console, 2) regression alerts tied to prompt-sets, 3) a small ops UX for managing prompt-sets. Need to decide minimum launch scope for the beta.
anya (product): +1 to prioritizing regression alerts — customers keep hitting silent quality regressions. If we only ship one thing, that should be it. :eyes:
mike (eng-ml): Agree regression alerts are high signal, but they’re also the most infra-heavy (eval pipeline, thresholds, drift detection). Batching/caching recs are smaller infra but a little fuzzy on ROI metrics.
carmen (eng-platform): From Dedicated/Private angle, caching recs need low-friction config export (YAML) so customers can apply on-prem. That adds product work but not heavy infra.
sam (devex): Prompt-set UX is the easiest visible win for self-serve customers — let them tag prompt-sets, store baselines, and run spot checks. Could be a light-weight MVP in 2 sprints.
kevin (pm): Proposed triage: ship a beta regression-alerts core + a lightweight prompt-set UX, postpone Console batching recs to scope-next quarter unless we can make caching recs purely advisory (docs + scoring) rather than config changes. Thoughts?
mike (eng-ml): Technical callouts: regression alerting needs: 1) automated eval runs on model/rollout, 2) baseline metric store, 3) alerting rules (static and percentile). If we limit to scheduled evals + basic threshold alerts we can make it 3 sprints.
anya (product): OK that sounds reasonable. Launch criteria idea: a) regression alerts trigger for >=2 customers in beta, b) ability to attach prompt-set baseline to an alert, c) docs + 3 quickstart templates. If those are green we call it GA candidate.
carmen (eng-platform): For the baseline store, prefer S3-backed versioning with metadata so Private customers can point to their KMS-backed buckets. That’s minor infra but important for compliance asks.
sam (devex): UI mock proposal: prompt-sets page with: upload, tag, baseline snapshot, run evaluation button. Keep it single-page to avoid scope creep. I can draft mock JSON now: ```{ "page": "prompt_sets", "actions": ["upload", "snapshot", "evaluate"] }```
kevin (pm): Nice. Can we break down dependencies + risk? Mike, list infra risks. Carmen, list platform deliverables. Sam, deliver a mock by EOD Friday. Anya, coordinate with sales for 3 beta customers.
mike (eng-ml): Infra risks: eval compute cost (need autoscale), metric drift false positives, data privacy handling for prompt-sets. Mitigations: cost cap per-customer, adjustable alert thresholds, ensure prompt-set upload has purge/delete flow.
carmen (eng-platform): Platform deliverables: 1) baseline artifact storage (S3-compatible), 2) RBAC for prompt-set access, 3) export CLI to pull baseline to on-prem. ETA: 3 sprints for basic feature set.
anya (product): I'll confirm 3 beta customers by EOD Wed. Also pushing on OKR tie: "Reduce customer-reported regressions by 30% Q4" — this feature maps directly.
kevin (pm): Decision for this thread: move forward with regression-alerts + prompt-set MVP for Q4 beta. Batch/caching recommendations will be advisory docs only in Q4, revisit in Q1 for Console integration. Action items: @mike infra spike (1 sprint), @sam mock + small usability test (1 sprint), @carmen platform spec (3 sprints), @anya beta commit.
ops-bot: Deploy plan created: `epic/optkit-regression-alerts` created and linked to ticket #PR-412.
sam (devex): Quick question — do we need a simple eval DSL or reuse current eval harness? I vote reuse harness and add a small wrapper for prompt-sets.
mike (eng-ml): Reuse harness. Add wrapper that normalizes prompt metadata. That keeps scope low.
kevin (pm): Great. I'll update roadmap slide and OKR doc with these decisions. If anyone has a major objection, flag here within 24h, otherwise I'll send the scope doc to eng leads tomorrow. :thumbsup:
anya (product): No objections from product. +1.
carmen (eng-platform): No blocking comments.
kevin (pm): Thanks all — closing thread.
